 Sreenidi Deccan Fc Face Fc Bengaluru United In Crucial Ifl Clash 
 Sreenidi Deccan FC face FC Bengaluru United in crucial IFL clash
 Sreenidi Deccan FC will look to recover from their previous defeat when they face FC Bengaluru United in the Indian Football League. The hosts, unbeaten at home, are targeting another victory to move into the top three
 By 
 Telangana Today 
 Published Date - 17 November 2026, 11:09 PM 
 Hyderabad : Sreenidi Deccan FC will look to bounce back from their previous-fixture defeat when they take on a confident FC Bengaluru United, who are unbeaten at home, in Match 16 of the Indian Football League (IFL) 2026-27 at the Bangalore Football Stadium in Bengaluru on Wednesday.
 The match will be telecast live on DD Sports and streamed on the Unite8 YouTube channel, Z5 and the WAVES app.
 Wednesday’s evening encounter will see promoted side FC Bengaluru United looking to consolidate their home form against a reinforced Sreenidi Deccan FC outfit that has spent the early weeks of the season negotiating a gruelling multi-city road trip.
 FC Bengaluru United, coached by Nallappan Mohanraj, will return to the Bangalore Football Stadium aiming to establish their home ground as a fortress in their debut Star Cement IFL campaign.
 The Bengaluru outfit has shown an eagerness to play on the front foot in familiar conditions and currently sits fifth in the standings with four points from three matches, following an entertaining 2-2 draw against Real Kashmir FC last Saturday.
 In that encounter, FC Bengaluru United fell behind early but responded with a moment of brilliance as Colombian playmaker Maikol Andres Herrera Casseres unleashed a stunning right-footed curling strike from distance to equalise. After falling behind again, the hosts pressed relentlessly until the final whistle and earned a point when Under-22 centre-back Abdul Hannan rose highest to head home a dramatic 90th-minute equaliser.
 Currently level on four points with their midweek opponents, a victory on Wednesday would break the deadlock and propel FC Bengaluru United into the top three.
 Speaking ahead of the midweek clash, FC Bengaluru United head coach Nallappan Mohanraj emphasised the importance of his side’s resilience and its ongoing adaptation to the top division.
 “A win is a win, and we would have been happy if we had got the three points. But the way we came back into the game, being 2-1 down and scoring in the 90th minute to get a point, we have to accept that fact because everyone worked together and fought well,” Mohanraj said.
 “As a coach at home, I would have liked to take all three points. But the way we fought for that one point made me very happy, and the boys deserved it.”
 Assessing the threat posed by Sreenidi Deccan FC, Mohanraj added: “As a newly promoted side in the Star Cement IFL, it takes time for many of our boys, who are playing at this level for the very first time, to settle into the intensity of the opposition. Sreenidi Deccan is a very good, experienced side and we are prepared to face them.
 “We are going to give everything from the first minute to the last. That is what we have prepared for, and that is the attitude and character the team is showing. It is our home game, and we have to push ourselves to the maximum.”
